block-string.comment: A block literal. Its escapes still escape, so it is the ordinary string rule with a longer delimiter; it is listed before `string` so the opening `"""` is not claimed as an empty literal followed by a quote.
block-string.name: string.quoted.triple.openepl

raw-block-string.comment: Raw: nothing inside is interpreted, so the body has no patterns at all — which is exactly the difference the highlighting should show.
raw-block-string.name: string.quoted.triple.raw.openepl

number.comment: Hex and binary bit patterns first, so `0xFF` is one number rather than `0` followed by a name. `_` groups digits.

patterns.comment: The name being declared is highlighted as an entity, not as a plain identifier — it is what the outline and go-to-definition target.
`on click do handler` binds an event to a subroutine.

statement-word.comment: The statement words that lead a block or a check. Like the bitwise operators they are soft keywords in the language — a variable may still be named for one — which a grammar this size cannot tell apart, so a name that collides is highlighted as the keyword.
statement-word.name: keyword.control.openepl

expression-word.comment: The words that join or guard a value: `then` for the `if` written as a value, `otherwise` for what a failure or an absent optional falls back to, `check` for the call that returns early, and `as` for the name `if some` binds. Soft keywords too, with the same caveat as above.
expression-word.name: keyword.control.openepl

member.comment: A name after `.` is a component property or event.
member.name: variable.other.property.openepl

indirect.comment: `call through fp(...)` calls a function pointer. `through` means that only straight after `call` — it is a soft keyword and a variable may still be named for it — so the pair is matched together rather than the word alone.

bitwise.comment: The bitwise operators are words. They are soft keywords in the language — a variable may be named for one — which a grammar this size cannot tell apart, so a name that collides is highlighted as the operator.
bitwise.name: keyword.operator.word.openepl

assignment.comment: A name on the left of `=` is an assignment target or a form property, never a type — `text = "hi"` must not highlight as the `text` type.
